title: Purpose of the business case practice
blurb: Explain what the business case practice is for: judging whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable.
question: A project board member asks why the business case keeps being reviewed after the project has been approved. Which purpose of the business case practice answers her?

teach.body: Formally: the business case practice establishes mechanisms to judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable, as a means of supporting decision-making about continued investment in it. In plain English: it gives the people paying for the project a reliable way to keep asking 'should we still be spending money on this?' and to get an honest answer.

teach.caption: Remember 'DVA': the three words in the official purpose.

teach.h: A plain-English way to read the three tests
head: Test
Ask yourself
Typical evidence
rows: Benefits set against costs, risks, dis-benefits
Can the project deliver the products?
Will the products lead to the benefits?
teach.caption: These glosses are a study aid; the exam tests the three words and the purpose itself.

teach.h: 'Is, and remains': a judgement that is repeated
teach.body: The purpose is not a one-off approval. Costs, risks, timescales and the business itself change, so the judgement is repeated: when starting up, when initiating, at every stage boundary, when an exception plan is assessed, and when significant issues or risks arise. Each time, the answer supports a decision about continued investment.

root.label: Is the project still desirable, viable and achievable?

children.label: Board considers stopping
children.sub: premature closure is a valid outcome

teach.body: Business justification is about value: the perceived benefits or importance of the outcomes in proportion to the resources used to achieve them, and choosing the option that offers the best overall value. Dis-benefits are part of the picture. The practice does not promise to prevent them; it makes sure they are identified and managed so the judgement stays honest.

values: A project needs a valid reason, kept valid
How to judge and record that reason

values: A rule that cannot be omitted
Mechanisms: business case, technique, approaches, roles

items: A business case documenting costs against benefits, offset by risks.
A technique to develop, check, maintain and confirm it.
A benefits management approach to measure and review benefits.
A sustainability management approach for sustainability targets.
Clear roles: the executive is accountable for the business case.

teach.body: Halden Library Service is installing self-service kiosks in 12 branches. Executive Martin Achebe approved the project on a strong business case. At the end of stage one, project manager Grace Lindqvist reports that kiosk prices have risen and a planned staff redeployment has been delayed. Using the updated business case, the board judges that the project is still desirable, viable and achievable, but asks for the benefits forecast to be revised before authorizing stage two.

teach.text: Classic trap: confusing the business case purpose with neighbouring practices. Defining the products to be delivered is plans; documenting the user's requirements is quality; forecasting progress against plans is progress. Second trap: the practice does not exist to prevent dis-benefits or guarantee benefits; it judges whether continued investment is justified.

items: Purpose: mechanisms to judge if the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable.
It supports decision-making about continued investment.
The judgement is repeated throughout, not made once.
Business justification is about value, not just cost.
Dis-benefits are identified and managed, not 'prevented'.

summary: You can now state the purpose of the business case practice and explain why the judgement of desirable, viable and achievable is repeated throughout the project. You can also tell it apart from the purposes of the plans, quality and progress practices.

A.q: What is the purpose of the business case practice?
options: To document the user's requirements and how they will be met
To judge whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable
To define the products and the means of delivering them
To identify, assess and control uncertainty for the project
A.why: The business case practice establishes mechanisms to judge whether the project is (and remains) desirable, viable and achievable, to support decisions on continued investment (manual 5.1).

whyNot.0: Documenting the user's requirements and how they will be met is the purpose of the quality practice.
whyNot.2: Defining the products and the means to deliver them is the purpose of the plans practice.
whyNot.3: Identifying, assessing and controlling uncertainty is the purpose of the risk practice.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The business case practice establishes mechanisms to judge whether the project is (and remains) desirable, [?] and achievable.
options: viable
affordable
compliant
sustainable
A.why: The official triplet is desirable, viable and achievable (manual 5.1).

whyNot.1: Affordability matters, but 'affordable' is not one of the three words in the purpose.
whyNot.2: Compliance may drive a project, but 'compliant' is not part of the purpose.
whyNot.3: Sustainability is a performance target; it is not one of the three words in the purpose.

A.q: The business case practice is a means of supporting decision-making about what?
options: The day-to-day allocation of work packages
The acceptance of each specialist product
Continued investment in the project
The selection of the project's team members
A.why: The judgement supports decision-making in the project's continued investment (manual 5.1).

whyNot.0: Allocating work packages is the project manager's job in controlling a stage.
whyNot.1: Product acceptance is governed by quality criteria and product descriptions.
whyNot.3: Appointing the team is part of the organizing practice and starting up a project.

B.q:
Which two statements about the purpose of the business case practice are correct?
1. Its purpose is to prevent any dis-benefits arising from the project.
2. It judges whether the project remains justified, not just whether it was at the start.
3. It defines the 'who' of the project.
4. Business justification is about value, not only cost.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: The purpose says the project 'is (and remains)' desirable, viable and achievable (2), and justification considers value: benefits in proportion to resources used (4).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is false: dis-benefits are identified and managed, not prevented.
whyNot.1: Both are false: dis-benefits are not prevented by the practice, and the 'who' belongs to organizing.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is false: the organizing practice defines the 'who'.

B.q: Which statement about dis-benefits and the business case practice is correct?
options: They are prevented before delivery starts
They are treated as project issues
They are a concern for the senior supplier
They are identified and then managed
B.why: It is not a purpose of the business case practice to prevent dis-benefits; they are identified and managed as part of judging the project (manual 5.1).

whyNot.0: The practice does not promise to prevent dis-benefits.
whyNot.1: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline from an outcome, not an issue as such.
whyNot.2: Dis-benefits affect the investing organization's business case, not the supplier's role.

B.q: Halfway through a project, the board wants a reliable way to decide whether further spending is still justified. Which practice provides the mechanism for this judgement?
options: Plans
Risk
Quality
Business case
B.why: The business case practice establishes the mechanisms to judge whether the project remains desirable, viable and achievable, supporting decisions on continued investment.

whyNot.0: Plans define the products and the means of delivering them.
whyNot.1: Risk controls uncertainty; it feeds the business case but does not judge continued investment.
whyNot.2: Quality covers the user's requirements and how they will be met.

C.q: Why does the purpose say the project 'is (and remains)' desirable, viable and achievable, and who mainly relies on this judgement?
options: It is rechecked throughout; the project board
It is rechecked throughout; the team managers
It is set once at the start; the project board
It is set once at the start; the business layer
C.why: Justification is checked repeatedly (at each decision point and when issues arise), and the project board uses it to decide whether to keep investing.

whyNot.1: Team managers deliver work packages; they do not make investment decisions.
whyNot.2: The board relies on it, but the judgement is repeated, not made once.
whyNot.3: The judgement is repeated, and the board makes the stage-by-stage investment decisions.

C.q: How does the business case practice relate to the 'ensure continued business justification' principle?
options: The practice states the need; the principle gives the mechanisms
The principle states the need; the practice gives the mechanisms
The principle covers compulsory projects; the practice does not
The principle can be tailored away; the practice cannot be tailored
C.why: The principle requires a justification that stays valid; the practice establishes the mechanisms (business case, technique, approaches, roles) to judge it.

whyNot.0: This reverses them: the principle is the rule, the practice is how it is applied.
whyNot.2: Compulsory projects still need a business case to justify the chosen option.
whyNot.3: Principles cannot be omitted; practices are what get tailored.

C.q: New regulations force a transport authority to upgrade its signalling. Which statement about the business case practice is correct for this project?
options: It is replaced by the regulator's ruling
It is used once to approve the budget
It is passed to the business layer to run
It still judges the option chosen to comply
C.why: Compulsory projects still need business justification, of the option chosen, and that justification is checked throughout like any other.

whyNot.0: A ruling removes the choice of whether to act, not the need to justify how.
whyNot.1: The judgement is repeated throughout, not made once.
whyNot.2: The executive is accountable for the business case within the project.

reteach.title: The car you keep paying for
reteach.question: If you were paying monthly for a car, what three things would make you keep paying?

blocks.body: You keep paying if the car is still worth the money, if the dealer can still supply what was promised, and if it still does the job you bought it for. PRINCE2 asks the same three questions of a project: desirable, viable and achievable. And just like your monthly payment, it asks them again at every decision point, not just on day one.

blocks.text: The practice supports decisions about continued investment. It does not define products (plans) or requirements (quality).

explain.body: The business case practice judges whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable.

test.q: Which three words describe what the business case practice judges?
options: Desirable, viable and achievable
Affordable, viable and compliant
Desirable, measurable and timely
Feasible, funded and approved
test.why: The official purpose uses desirable, viable and achievable (manual 5.1).

whyNot.1: 'Affordable' and 'compliant' are not in the purpose.
whyNot.2: 'Measurable' and 'timely' are not in the purpose.
whyNot.3: These are not the official three words.

explain.body: The judgement is made at the start and repeated throughout the project, because costs, risks and the business change.

test.q: When does the business case practice judge whether the project is justified?
options: At initiation and at closure
At the start and throughout
When the mandate is issued
After benefits are realized
test.why: The purpose says 'is (and remains)': the judgement is repeated throughout.

whyNot.0: It is also repeated at every stage boundary, not just at these two points.
whyNot.2: The mandate triggers starting up; the judgement continues long after.
whyNot.3: Waiting until benefits are realized is too late to guide investment.

explain.body: Business justification is about the value of the outcomes in proportion to the resources used, choosing the option of best overall value.

test.q: Which statement about business justification is correct?
options: It is based on the lowest project cost
It compares project cost with its budget
It weighs value against resources used
It is measured by products delivered
test.why: Business justification is about value: benefits or importance of outcomes in proportion to the resources used (manual 5.1).

whyNot.0: The cheapest option is not necessarily the best value.
whyNot.1: Budget tracking is progress control, not justification.
whyNot.3: Products are outputs; justification is about the value they lead to.

explain.body: Defining what will be delivered and how is the plans practice. The business case practice judges whether delivering it is worth the investment.

test.q: A board member says the business case practice exists to define what products will be delivered. Which practice actually has that purpose?
options: Plans
Quality
Progress
Issues
test.why: Plans define the products to be delivered (the 'what') and the means to deliver them (manual 7.1).

whyNot.1: Quality documents the user's requirements of the products and how they will be met.
whyNot.2: Progress compares actual achievement with plans and controls deviations.
whyNot.3: Issues collects and assesses issues and controls changes to baselines.
